content.title: Tyson Foods says it has succession plans after executive's shock departure
content.summary: CHICAGO (Reuters) -Tyson Foods sought to reassure investors that it has succession plans in place on Thursday, after announcing this week that an executive seen by some analysts as a possible future CEO left the company over conduct violations.  The meatpacker said late on Tuesday that Chief Supply Chain Officer Brady Stewart, who has also overseen its beef, pork and prepared foods businesses, ran afoul of its code of conduct.  Tyson representatives have not responded to questions about the violations.

content.title: Tyson Foods says supply-chain chief leaves after violating conduct rules
content.summary: CHICAGO (Reuters) -Tyson Foods' chief supply chain officer, who has also overseen its beef, pork and prepared foods businesses, left the U.S. meatpacker after violating the company's code of conduct, according to a statement.  The departure of Brady Stewart is the latest management change at Tyson Foods, which replaced former Chief Financial Officer John R. Tyson last year following arrests related to drinking.  Stewart could not immediately be reached for comment on Wednesday.
